claim_boundary: Breaks what each guard watches and records whether the guard failed. Runs no backtest, opens no return data, registers no hypothesis identity, and changes nothing permanently — every mutation is restored and the restoration is verified by hash. 0 trials.
coverage_is_derived: The guard set is computed from tests/unit by the same rule every run, so a guard added without a mutation appears here rather than joining the unmutated majority unnoticed.

ledger.mutation: raise the Newey-West t floor above what the deflated-Sharpe floor can reach
notes: The unsatisfiable-floors class: two gates that cannot both be met.

ledger.mutation: add a threshold the evaluator does not read
notes: A threshold sitting in the contract wearing a gate's costume.

ledger.mutation: move the published Sharpe target away from the correlation it requires
notes: First aimed at average_pairwise_correlation_objective, which this guard does not read: it watches the GATE and the target. A mutation that misses is indistinguishable from a guard that cannot fail, and that is the whole trap this ledger exists inside.

ledger.mutation: loosen the out-of-sample observation minimum
change the contract the site derives its published gate summary from
corrupt the declared live-configuration fingerprint
notes: The ceremony that stopped a live sizing change contaminating the forward record.

ledger.mutation: publish a clone URL for a repository that does not exist
notes: The defect that actually shipped, reproduced.

ledger.mutation: stop the hourly deploy announcing what it published
reorder the publish pipeline so a contract is copied before it is rebuilt
notes: The stale-artifact class: research_export copies whatever is on disk.

ledger.mutation: label the chain's ENTRY count with the word days on the published page
notes: The count-is-not-a-duration defect, reproduced: this exact wording once overstated a 47-day chain as 371 days. First aimed at the chain FILE, which this guard does not read — it watches what the page calls the number.

ledger.mutation: edit a published artifact after it was hashed
notes: Exactly what the reproduce kit exists to detect, done from the inside.

ledger.mutation: let a published contract go stale against its source
make the generator print a figure the kill-log entry does not contain
notes: Two earlier attempts moved the kill log itself and were not caught, and that is CORRECT rather than a gap: this guard regenerates each paper from the entry, so moving the entry moves both sides together. What it actually watches is the GENERATOR, which is what research_export.py runs on every publish. The mutation therefore has to break the generator.

ledger.mutation: drop the KILLED disclosure from a sleeve whose artifact records that verdict
notes: Two earlier attempts moved NUMBERS in the artifacts; this guard watches DISCLOSURE LANGUAGE — that a killed sleeve is described as killed — so a number is the wrong thing to move.

ledger.mutation: double the live gross target this sleeve trades at
let non-equity instruments back into the equity target book
notes: The unscoped-universe defect that put perpetuals in an equity artifact.

ledger.mutation: change the curve transform away from the log basis every consumer assumes
stop the LIVE broker booking funding
notes: The carry sleeve booked funding zero times in 44 days once, because a TypeError was swallowed by a bare except and nine tests pinned the intention rather than the path.

ledger.mutation: NEGATIVE CONTROL: edit a comment and nothing else
notes: THE HARNESS'S NEGATIVE CONTROL. This edits a COMMENT and nothing else, so the guard must NOT fail. A mutation harness with no control looks perfect precisely when it is broken: if every run reports CAUGHT, the reason might be that the runner fails for reasons unrelated to the mutation.

ledger.mutation: make the lineage audit return PASS unconditionally
notes: Two earlier attempts moved DATA; this guard runs the audit over fixtures, so it watches the audit's LOGIC. A gate that always passes is the thing to break.

negative_controls.mutation: NEGATIVE CONTROL: edit a comment and nothing else
notes: THE HARNESS'S NEGATIVE CONTROL. This edits a COMMENT and nothing else, so the guard must NOT fail. A mutation harness with no control looks perfect precisely when it is broken: if every run reports CAUGHT, the reason might be that the runner fails for reasons unrelated to the mutation.

why: A check that cannot fail is worse than no check: it produces the confidence of a guard with none of the protection, and a passing test looks identical whether it is watching something or nothing.
